title: A Provision for the Monsoon
premise: Casper Nakamura runs cargo upriver on the Kestrel, a patched riverboat crewed by a found family he refuses to name as such, because names and roots are how the past collects debts. When a government survey team vanishes above the gorge, leaving instruments running and no tracks, the colonial administration conscripts Casper to ferry a search party — including surveyor Ada Okonkwo, who carries the dead team's sealed inheritance: land grants that could dispossess the river villages or save them. As sabotage, flood, and a rival salvage crew close in, Casper must choose between the anonymity he's bought with twenty years of moving and the people who keep choosing him. The crew crosses the range ahead of the snows and beats the monsoon's landfall by hours, delivering the grants to the villages, and Casper finally stops — mooring the Kestrel for good, not as surrender, but as home.
about_author: Mirabel Quintana is the pen name of a former hydrographic technician who spent six seasons charting monsoon-fed rivers before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose maps and their hearts disagree.

chapters.title: The Sandbar's Mood
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine cargo run up the Kestrel River establishes the boat, the crew — engineer Bao, deckhand twins Sefa and Lio, cook Marisol — and Casper's rule: never stay anywhere longer than the water level. When he quietly pays off a village elder's debt and leaves before dawn, we feel the cost of his rootlessness. Beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Paper from the Capital
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A colonial administrator conscripts the Kestrel: a government survey team has gone silent above Widow's Gorge, and Casper's knowledge of every sandbar makes him the only captain who can reach them before the season turns. He refuses; the administrator invokes an old debt Casper thought buried. Beat: the past arrives wearing official letterhead.

chapters.title: The Surveyor with the Sealed Case
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Surveyor Ada Okonkwo boards with a locked instrument case and orders she won't share. She's the vanished team's cartographer, sent to finish or recover their work, and she clocks immediately that the crew functions like a family no one will admit to. First friction with Casper over route and risk. Beat: two guarded people measuring each other.

chapters.title: Instruments Still Running
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The team's last camp is found intact — kettle warm, instruments logging, no tracks, no blood. Ada decodes the final survey entries: they'd found something in the high valley worth hiding. Casper notices someone has paid a downstream informant to watch the Kestrel. Beat: dread replacing mystery.

chapters.title: The Rival on the Water
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A salvage crew under Captain Voss shadows them — hired, Casper realizes, by the same interests who want the survey's findings buried. A tense sandbar standoff ends in a collision that cracks the Kestrel's hull. Beat: the river itself becomes contested territory.

chapters.title: What the Case Contains
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Forced to open the case after floodwater threatens it, Ada reveals the truth: the vanished team mapped land grants that legally belong to the river villages — inheritance papers that could undo a generation of dispossession, or be destroyed. The crew votes to carry on. Casper abstains. Beat: found family choosing a cause.

chapters.title: Marisol's Story
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Repairs at a mid-river village; Marisol, the crew's heart, reveals she was dispossessed by the same land syndicate, and why she cooks for a crew that won't call itself one. Casper listens and says nothing, but that night he repairs Sefa's broken compass instead of replacing it. Beat: tenderness as repair.

chapters.title: The Gorge Portage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Kestrel must be winched through Widow's Gorge's rapids in pieces — the book's first set-piece. Voss's men sabotage a winch line mid-portage; Lio nearly drowns; Casper's river-craft saves him. The crew stops calling the boat 'the boat.' Beat: the Kestrel becomes a character worth dying for.

chapters.title: Snow Line
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Above the gorge, the terrain turns alpine. Ada's instruments show the monsoon will make landfall in eleven days; the pass closes with snow in nine. The arithmetic is brutal and public, and Casper, for the first time, plans a route he cannot scout alone. Beat: humility as the price of trust.

chapters.title: The Herder's Pass
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A mountain herder, Old Yeva, offers a goat track over the range in exchange for the Kestrel's cargo of salt — a payment Casper makes without haggling, shocking the crew. Yeva warns that someone bought her silence last week. Beat: Casper begins paying forward instead of paying off.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss corners Ada at a ridge camp: deliver the case, and the syndicate will make her the empire's chief cartographer — every map, every name, in her hand. She refuses, but Casper overhears enough to doubt her, an old wound reopening. Beat: love against duty takes its first casualty — trust.

chapters.title: The Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Lio's POV. A storm strands them above the tree line. Huddled in a snow cave, the crew tells the stories they've never told — how each of them came aboard — and Casper, pressed, gives up a piece of his: a brother lost to the syndicate's floods, the reason he keeps moving. Beat: intimacy at altitude.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Col
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The syndicate's agent is among them — not Ada, but Bao, whose family the syndicate still holds. He takes the case at the col and descends toward Voss. Casper's instinct is to cut losses and turn back; instead he orders the crew after Bao. Beat: the captain chooses people over survival math.

chapters.title: Descent into the Cloud Forest
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. A harrowing off-trail descent to intercept Bao — leeches, fog, a rope bridge that fails. They catch him, and Bao, broken, confesses the syndicate holds his sister. Ada proposes a plan that uses the case itself as bait. Beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: The False Case
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada forges a decoy case with doctored grant papers that would implicate Voss in theft if opened. The crew stages a camp ambush; Voss takes the bait and the real case stays hidden in Marisol's flour barrel. Beat: the family's small skills — cooking, cartography, knots — become the weapon.

chapters.title: Monsoon's Edge
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Landfall is now hours, not days. The syndicate's real buyer arrives by airboat on the flooded lower river, and Voss, discovering the forgery, goes rogue — burning his employers' contract and hunting the Kestrel out of pride. Beat: the antagonist becomes desperate, and more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Last Rapid
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The set-piece: the Kestrel, patched and overloaded, races the rising river through the gorge's final rapid with Voss's boat behind and the monsoon's first rain falling. Casper reads the sandbars' moods one last time and threads a channel no chart shows. Beat: mastery and love fused in one run of white water.

chapters.title: What Voss Wanted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss, wrecked on a shoal, is pulled from the water by the crew he hunted. In the aftermath she admits she was the syndicate's mapmaker once too — that she knows exactly what it is to be owned. Casper lets her come with them, unarmed. Beat: the enemy unmasked as a mirror.

chapters.title: The Valley of the Grants
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They reach the survey team — alive, snowbound, protecting the valley's villagers who had sheltered them. The grants are read aloud in the village square as the monsoon breaks in full: rain like a curtain, and the papers countersigned before the ink could run. Beat: catharsis; inheritance delivered.

chapters.title: Debts and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The administrator arrives to arrest someone; Ada produces the syndicate's own forged papers, implicating the capital. Bao's sister is freed in the ensuing inquiry. Casper realizes the debt that conscripted him has been paid — by the family, not by him. Beat: freedom arriving from an unexpected direction.

chapters.title: Moorings
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The crew refits the Kestrel at the village through the long rains. Casper, who has never stayed past a season, signs the boat over to the crew collectively and stays — repairing the village jetty, learning names. Ada stays too, mapping the valley for the villages instead of the empire. Beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty.

chapters.title: A Provision for the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A year later, the monsoon returns and finds the valley provisioned — grain stored, grants held, the Kestrel moored and crewed by people who chose each other. Casper teaches Sefa the sandbars' moods, passing the river on. Final line lands on the theme: stopping, he finally understands, was never the cost. It was the provision. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
